correctness.rationale: Verified RESULT.md lines 28–95. In z=kx, the projection Jacobian for intrinsic area is √(1+k²), and the projected radial cutoff is r/(1+(kr/h)|cos θ|), giving A=r²√(1+(ha/r)²)I(a). The horizontal disk and vertical diamond have areas πr² and 2rh. Substituting s=tan θ gives I(a)=2∫₀^∞(a+√(1+s²))^(−2)ds; replacing its denominator by 1+(a+s)² strictly increases the integral for a>0. I independently checked the second strict inequality without a product identity. Put x=1/a and g(x)=x/√(1+4x²/π²)−arctan x. Then g(0)=g(∞)=0; the sign of g′ is opposite to that of H(x²)=(1+4x²/π²)^(3/2)−1−x². H is strictly convex in x², has negative initial slope 6/π²−1 and tends to infinity, so g increases then decreases and is strictly positive for finite x>0. The frozen partial-fraction proof is valid as well: each positive-degree tangent coefficient is ≥8/π²>1/2, which dominates the corresponding reciprocal-square-root coefficient. Hence the asserted elliptic envelope holds strictly. It is sharp at zero and infinity; at infinity rescaling s=av in the first integral gives aI(a)→2 by domination with 2/(1+v)². Comparing the envelope multiplied by the Jacobian with the winning endpoint immediately yields the three equality regimes, with no oblique equality including at h/r=π/2. The closed forms follow from I/2=J+aJ′ for J=∫(1+a cos θ)^(−1)dθ evaluated by tan(θ/2); the a=1 limit is 4/3. An independent orthonormal-plane polar midpoint calculation at r=1, h=1.21, a=0.73 gave area 2.119479139, versus 2.119479141 from the projected polar formula. Inspected VERIFICATION.md and check_bicone.py; did not run the uploaded script. Finite quadrature illustrates the formula and does not establish the strict continuum bound. No assertion about noncentral, noncircular or higher-dimensional sections was checked.

value.rationale: The orientation optimization is a natural geometric problem; comparing the two obvious sections alone does not show that one is best. The strict envelope supplies the obstruction to any interior maximizing direction at the tie aspect ratio and gives a complete sharp classification for every aspect ratio. This matters separately from the known profile or computations of its minimum.
